messages:
jordan: Heads-up — seeing p99 spikes right after autoscale events on prod-nyc pool. p95 stays ~120ms but p99 jumps to ~1.2s for ~30s after scale-up. Noticed this across a few model families.
megan: ugh. do we know if it's kernel warmup or KV misses? any flamegraphs? :thinking_face:
ravi: Initial profiling suggests two things: 1) cold KV cache leads to repeated disk reads for shard metadata, 2) the kernel selector falls back to the generic matmul path for some sequence-length combos after node join. both add latency.
jordan: exact numbers from last incident: traffic ramp 0 -> 400 qps, autoscaler added 6 nodes in 15s. p99 timeline: 1.2s spike for ~28s, then decays. CPU on nodes that just joined shows higher memcpy+cuda-launch time.
megan: posting quick perf output from the canary:
```
# perf slice (summary)
kernel_fast_attention  avg 0.9ms  p99 1.1ms
kernel_generic_matmul  avg 3.5ms p99 12.4ms
kv_cache_miss_read    avg 4.2ms  p99 120ms
```
megan: huge delta in kv_cache_miss p99. if many requests hit new nodes with empty KV, tail balloons.
anna: (typo: anna — but keep consistent) we should treat cold-starts as two-axis problem: compute kernel warmup + KV coldness. Pre-warming kernels (touching kernels with a synthetic request) helps latency but costs warmup ops.
ravi: alternative: adaptive microbatch sizing. If queue depth low but node just joined, force microbatch=1 to avoid waiting; if queue depth high, increase batch to 8. microbatch tuning changed p95/p99 tradeoff in perf lab earlier.
miguel: note we shipped runtime change -> kernel selector now prefers simd-fused kernels for seq<=256. that commit (git:abc123) inadvertently misses a path where seq==257 -> falls to generic. regression landed in last release.
jordan: ah ok. that explains sudden p99 for models that often cross chunk boundaries. can we add a kernel fallback with warm compilation?
megan: short-term mitigations I can push: (1) pre-warm new nodes with a lightweight synthetic request that primes KV and touches optimized kernels, (2) change autoscaler to add 1s delay before routing traffic to brand-new nodes while we pre-warm. both are config flips.
megan: config snippet I tested in staging: 
```
autoscale:
  prewarm_requests: 2
  node_warm_delay_s: 1.5
batching:
  microbatch_min: 1
  microbatch_target: 4
  adaptive: true
```
anna: also propose per-kernel latency histograms exported to console so routing can prefer warmed nodes for tail-sensitive routes. expose p95/p99 per kernel + kv hit rate.
ravi: tradeoff summary: increasing microbatch target reduces CPU/GPU kernel overhead and improves throughput, but adds jitter to tail for single-request flows. reducing microbatch hurts throughput and cost. need SLO-based rule: for latency-SLO routes (p95<200ms) bias toward microbatch=1; for throughput routes, bias up.
miguel: will open a revert PR for abc123 and a small fix to selector to handle off-by-one seq buckets. canary tomorrow.
jordan: can we also add a tiny KV cache prefill for shard metadata on node bring-up? even reading the index into memcached would knock down kv_cache_miss to microseconds.
megan: yes, I have a patch that does an async prefetch on node init. it reduces kv_miss p99 from 120ms->6ms in staging. will roll to prod in canary ring after miguel's selector fix.
sre-bot: ALERT: autoscale_p99_spike detected 2026-03-16T12:23:45Z for pool prod-nyc. linked thread 1761234567. suggested actions: prewarm nodes, enable selector fix canary, monitor kernel p99 metrics. :warning:
jordan: next steps: 1) miguel revert + fix selector 2) megan enable prewarm+node_warm_delay in autoscaler 3) megan roll KV prefetch canary 4) anna add per-kernel histo dashboards. schedule: canary tonight, full roll tomorrow if green.
megan: I'll run a 10k qps load test with traffic spikes to validate. will paste profiling dump and flamegraph link here when done. :thumbsup:
